To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a neural network model can: 1. Learn representations that are grammatically interpretable.

(1) the TPRN architecture can be applied to the question answering task with no loss in accuracy; (2) internal representations learned by the TPRN are interpretable in a linguistically meaningful way, and (3) the interpretation of the learned representations can be used to gain insights about the model, and to provide a more detailed explanation of its performance

(i) the TPRN model can learn to perform a complex QA task, (ii) the internal representations of the model can be interpreted as a composition of symbols and roles, (iii) the model can be used to interpret the symbols and roles, and (iv) the model's symbols can be interpreted using lexical semantic information, and the roles can be interpreted using grammatical role categories.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning to interpret the internal representation of a deep neural network trained for a natural language understanding task, using linguistic theory as a guide.
developing a deep neural network model which is both interpretable and performant.
the question: what does the model learn, when it learns to answer questions about text, without being given linguistic knowledge?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TPRN model learns to use symbols and roles to perform question answering, and that these can be interpreted as word meanings and grammatical roles, respectively.

the model is able to learn to build grammatically interpretable representations, which can be used to answer questions, without prior linguistic knowledge, and that the learned representations are in some sense grammatically correct.
we have shown that it is possible to learn a representation that is interpretable in terms of linguistic theory and that performs comparably to state of the art models on the SQuAd QA task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model learns to represent text using discrete symbols and roles.
we have developed a model that can learn to build grammatically interpretable representations from text, without being explicitly given the grammar.
a deep neural network can be used as a black box to perform a complex task, or can be interpreted in order to learn about how the network performs that task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TPRN architecture can learn interpretable representations, and that such representations are useful for question answering.

a neural network can learn to build representations which can be interpreted in terms of basic concepts from linguistic and cognitive theory, without being given any linguistic knowledge, and without any performance penalty.
a model which is designed in a linguistically interpretable manner can be trained to perform a complex linguistic task without any prior linguistic knowledge.
